clue.text: A good one might let one off

definitions.text: A good one might let one off

parts.words: A good one might let one off
parts.note: a convincing reason offered for a lapse may get the offender released from blame or punishment

explanation.surface: Something kind that might spare a person a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A plausible justification can persuade someone to pardon a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Guess the value of a property divided by the return of the motorway

indicators.note: divided by says the property word is split open by the road

parts.note: an estate is landed property

indicators.note: the return of means the road abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main motorway, read as MI

explanation.surface: Valuing a house split by a new road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the return of' reads the road backwards and 'divided by' splits the property word open. The M1 is Britain's first major motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge an approximate worth or amount.

clue.text: Minister likes his tea without milk or sugar

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
plain describes something with nothing added

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes his tea black.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution.

clue.text: Narrow bit of land the depth of one spade

definitions.meaning: a thin point of land jutting into water
a gardener's measure, one blade's depth of soil

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a thin promontory and a spade's depth of digging.

clue.text: Make notes about young fish fighting

indicators.note: about says the music-making word goes round the fish word

parts.note: to make musical notes is to sing
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: Someone humming tunes around baby fish while scrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' looks like jotting things down, but it means singing; 'about' wraps that round the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparring is practice boxing, a form of combat.

clue.text: Hastens arrival of rain

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both hurries something on and falls as rain from the sky.

clue.text: Horse which sped round the ring

indicators.note: round says the past-tense verb surrounds the circle

parts.note: sped means ran
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A horse galloping around the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat is flecked with white.

clue.text: Sound in perception

parts.note: tact is sensitive perception of others' feelings

explanation.surface: Being astute and sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact means whole and undamaged, as sound does.

clue.text: Travel wildly about to get a contraption of some sort

parts.note: to gad about is to roam restlessly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Roaming aimlessly to obtain some device.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small mechanical device.

clue.text: Soldier got caught in overturned cart-it was extremely sad

indicators.note: got caught in says the soldier word ends up inside the vehicle word
overturned means the word cart is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier trapped under an upturned cart: a terrible scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reads the vehicle backwards, and 'got caught in' traps the soldier inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tragic is deeply sorrowful or calamitous.

clue.text: Left when some were caught in the act

indicators.note: were caught in says the portion word sits within the deed word

parts.note: an act is a deed
some means a part of something

explanation.surface: People slipped away when a few were caught red-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'were caught in' traps the portion inside the act; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed is a past tense for went away.

clue.text: It's difficult to illustrate magnesium for him

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters are troubled into another order

parts.note: Mg is the chemical symbol for magnesium

explanation.surface: A scientist finds depicting magnesium hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' signals the anagram of ILLUSTRATE plus MG. 'him' points to the specialist the clue imagines working with magnesium.
explanation.definitionFit: A metallurgist is a scientist who studies metals such as magnesium.

clue.text: Man who takes many a drink

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large number
ale is a drink of beer

explanation.surface: A fellow who downs plenty of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Male describes a man or a member of the masculine sex.

clue.text: Tries again in the exam

parts.note: a student who failed a test sits it a second time

explanation.surface: A student having another go at the examination.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a failed examination a second time is a repeat sitting.

clue.text: After reaching a hundred, he got a pain

indicators.note: after reaching places the pronoun after the first pieces

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written

explanation.surface: A batsman reaching his century, then feeling sore.
explanation.walkthrough: HE comes after A and C (a hundred), as 'After reaching' says.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull, lasting pain.

clue.text: Don returns to bed…

indicators.note: returns means the phrase for being in bed is read backwards

parts.note: someone gone to bed is not up

explanation.surface: An academic goes back to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Gone to bed means NOT UP; 'returns' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to dress in them.

clue.text: … while Hank's excited by symbols of life

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: the name with its S used as letters

explanation.surface: A man named Hank is thrilled by emblems of life.
explanation.definitionFit: An ankh is the ancient Egyptian looped cross representing life.

clue.text: Afflictions which often follow trials

parts.note: the stock phrase trials and ... puts the troubles straight after the word trials

explanation.surface: Distress that comes after court cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribulations are troubles and suffering, paired with trials in a common idiom.

clue.text: Attract many to choose at random

parts.note: to draw a crowd is to attract it
lots means many

explanation.surface: Pulling in a crowd to decide by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing lots is picking by chance from tokens.

clue.text: Lady whose horse took early lead, then gave everything up

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

indicators.note: lead means the opening letter of the word early
up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A woman whose horse led from the start then flagged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ALL into LLA; 'lead' gives E from 'early'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabella is a woman's name.

clue.text: Absent minded sheep farmer?

parts.note: a daydreamer is said to be collecting fleece, which a shepherd might literally do

explanation.surface: A forgetful shepherd.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolgathering is idle daydreaming, so someone doing it is distracted.

clue.text: Sailor accustomed to being sworn at

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
used to means accustomed to

explanation.surface: A sailor used to being cursed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abused can mean being insulted verbally.

clue.text: Cartel makes wine

indicators.note: makes suggests the letters are made into something else

explanation.surface: A cartel produces wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is red wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: Dance round

definitions.meaning: a formal social gathering for dancing

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a formal dancing party and a sphere.

clue.text: Went right in but couldn't remember what to say

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for passed away

parts.note: went, as in passed on, means died

explanation.surface: An actor stepped on stage but forgot the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who dries forgets the lines mid-performance, theatrical slang.

clue.text: Quarters a sailor has to mop out

parts.note: S for south is a compass quarter
W for west is another compass quarter
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor in his quarters must clean the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To swab is to clean a deck with a wet cloth.

clue.text: Ready for business, but pen has no ink!

parts.note: with no ink the pen gives nothing, a zero shape
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shop's open, but its pen is dry.
explanation.definitionFit: An open shop is trading.

clue.text: Drink made from pears which can be ripe

annotationWithheld.why: 'Drink made from pears which can be ripe' (4) for PERI: the clue sounds like perry and rearranges ripe, but no word defines PERI, a fairy; definition apparently missing
annotationWithheld.clue: Drink made from pears which can be ripe

clue.text: Phrase I'm using to describe angelic host

indicators.note: using here signals the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Words chosen to describe a heavenly choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' signals the anagram of PHRASE and IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphim are the highest order of angels, a heavenly company.

clue.text: A month back got two ducks than a fifty-must be trick!

indicators.note: back means the month abbreviation is read in the other direction

parts.note: Feb is February
a duck is a zero score in cricket, O, so two give OO
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A cricketer gets two noughts then a half-century: surely a hoax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns FEB into BEF. A duck is a score of nought in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To befool is to fool or deceive someone.

clue.text: Set off for school in time

indicators.note: in places the school name inside the word for a time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Leaving for school on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the school inside the time word. Eton is a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to make it explode.

clue.text: After lunch nap is a set requirement

indicators.note: the word asks for a new arrangement of the letters given just before it

explanation.surface: A post-lunch snooze is obligatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IS A SET are rearranged; 'requirement' serves as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is a short rest taken in the early afternoon.
